newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended a volatile session on Tuesday with solid gains, but off highs, and underperforming the German market, traders said.
But trade was sluggish ahead of public holidays on Thursday and Friday and a flurry of U.S. economic data this week.

"Tomorrow I'd expect the market to trade sideways, with profit-taking likely to emerge in the afternoon. I guess no one wants to go on holiday without being either short or covered," a Madrid-based dealer said.
He added that the long term future had strong resistance at 113.60 and then at 113.80.

"For tomorrow I don't not expect any major movement in our market. Morning trade will be determined by today's close in U.S. Treasuries, and in the afternoon people will close their books," another dealer said.

Earlier on Tuesday, bonos jumped ahead with Bunds after U.S. Q1 labour costs rose 0.6 percent, less than the expected 0.9 percent. Dealers said the market was eagerly awaiting further data this week for signs of the true state of the U.S. economy.
In the longer run, dealers were bullish saying Spain's fundamentals supported further gains in the first half of May.
